negative_findings.description: Direct WebFetch of https://bqk-kos.org/?lang=sr returned HTTP 403 Forbidden, so the Serbian-language section structure of the CBK site could not be enumerated in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: 403 on the regulator's own Serbian-language landing page; the site is clearly live (search engines index SRB-*.pdf regulation files under /wp-content/uploads/2025/12/), so this reads as bot defence, not a dead host. Recorded as unverified, not dead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The single most important source in this cell cannot be collected with a naive fetcher; the collection pipeline needs a browser-like agent or an allowlisted crawler, otherwise the entire Serbian-language regulatory feed silently returns nothing.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated Serbian-language public-consultation portal or consultation register for CBK draft regulations was located.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches in Serbian for CBK consultation terms surfaced only news coverage of finished decisions, not a konsultacije/javna rasprava page in Serbian. Kosovo's central government consultation platform (konsultimet.rks-gov.net) was not confirmed to carry CBK items or Serbian translations in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If draft CBK rules are consulted only in Albanian, Serbian-language monitoring will always be reactive — catching rules after adoption rather than during the comment window, which is precisely the deadline intelligence this workstream needs.

negative_findings.description: The Office of the Language Commissioner's canonical domain was not confirmed by a successful fetch.
negative_findings.result_summary: The institution and its 2024 complaint statistics were confirmed through KoSSev and UNS reporting, but its own website URL (zkgjnj.rks-gov.net) is inferred from the rks-gov.net naming convention and must be resolved by the verification pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This source is the structural indicator of Serbian-language publication compliance; an unresolved URL means the pipeline would fall back on second-hand media reporting only.

negative_findings.description: No Ombudsperson Institution (OIK) report or ex-officio case specifically on the Regulation on Cash Operations was found in Serbian.
negative_findings.result_summary: Search combining Ombudsman, Serbian-language report and cash-operations regulation terms returned only generic institutional pages; no matching document surfaced.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: An OIK opinion would be the most authoritative non-partisan assessment of the regulation's effect on Serb-majority municipalities; its apparent absence (or non-indexing) means this angle is currently covered only by advocacy sources on both sides.

negative_findings.description: No consistent Serbian-language terminology was found for CBK supervisory/enforcement actions against unlicensed payment providers.
negative_findings.result_summary: Enforcement in Serb-majority areas is reported in police/political vocabulary ('zatvorene filijale', 'zaplenjeno', 'nelegalna finansijska institucija') rather than supervisory vocabulary ('oduzimanje licence', 'nadzorna mera', 'sankcija'), so keyword lists built from supervisory terms will miss most events.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Keyword design for this cell must use police/political Serbian vocabulary alongside regulatory vocabulary, or enforcement events will be systematically under-collected.

coverage_gaps.description: It is unknown how complete and how timely the Serbian-language mirror of CBK regulations, consultations and deadline notices actually is relative to the Albanian original.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a parity monitor: enumerate CBK regulation PDFs by language prefix (SRB-*, Albanian, ENG-*) and record, per instrument, whether a Serbian version exists and its publication lag in days.

coverage_gaps.description: No confirmed Serbian-language channel for draft regulations under consultation was found, leaving the pipeline able to see only adopted acts.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Investigate konsultimet.rks-gov.net for CBK entries and language variants; if absent, treat the CBK Serbian news feed plus KoSSev as the only early-warning proxies and flag consultation coverage as structurally weak for sr.

coverage_gaps.description: Kosovo-licensed commercial banks (e.g. NLB Banka, Raiffeisen Kosovo, TEB, ProCredit, Banka Ekonomike) were not profiled for Serbian-language customer communications, branch/ATM rollout in the four northern municipalities, or mobile banking units — yet they are the entities that had to operationalise the euro-only rule.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a dedicated pass over Kosovo commercial bank sites and the Kosovo Banking Association (Shoqata e Bankave të Kosovës) checking for Serbian-language pages, northern branch/ATM network announcements and fee schedules for currency exchange.

coverage_gaps.description: No statistical or supervisory dataset was identified that quantifies cash/currency-exchange volumes or banking penetration specifically in Serb-majority municipalities.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Check CBK statistics/financial-stability reports and the Kosovo Agency of Statistics for municipality-level financial indicators, and NBS reports for dinar volumes designated for Kosovo; record explicitly if no municipality-level breakdown exists.

coverage_gaps.description: Most retrieved Serbian material was Latin-script; NBS and some Serbian-state sources publish in Cyrillic (e.g. the NBS media-questions page on unilateral measures).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Ensure all Serbian keyword lists are duplicated in Cyrillic (динар, платни промет, Народна банка Србије, Централна банка Косова) and that transliteration-normalising matching is applied at collection time.

coverage_gaps.description: Most confirmed evidence clusters around the Jan-May 2024 introduction and enforcement wave; the current (2025-2026) state of enforcement, any amendments to the Regulation on Cash Operations, and the fate of a dinar payment workaround are not established.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a recency-scoped follow-up sweep in Serbian for 2025-2026 amendments, CBK licensing decisions for the north, and outcomes of EU-facilitated dialogue on payments.

brief: The Serbian-language layer of Kosovo's payments regulation is real and collectible, but it is split across three disconnected tiers: the CBK's own ?lang=sr / SRB-*.pdf document track (authoritative, bot-defended, and of unproven completeness versus the Albanian original), a dense Kosovo Serb media layer in the north and the enclaves (KoSSev, Kosovo Online, Radio Kontakt Plus, Radio KIM, Goraždevac, aggregated by Kosinfo) that is often the only reporter of actual enforcement and of continued dinar circulation, and a Belgrade counter-institutional tier (NBS, Poštanska štedionica, Kancelarija za KiM, Tanjug/RTS) documenting the parallel payment channel that Kosovo Police dismantled in 2024. The single highest-value structural finding is that Serbian-language coverage is itself a monitored compliance question: the Language Commissioner logged around 40 language-law complaints in 2024, so publication lag in Serbian must be measured, not assumed. The main blind spots are consultation-stage documents in Serbian, the Kosovo commercial-bank layer that had to implement the euro-only rule in the north, and anything after mid-2024.
